To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the experimental uncertainty in Newton's constant is as large as or larger than the uncertainties in helioseismic measurements of the solar sound speed, but the two can be combined to yield a test of G with an accuracy that is comparable to or even better than the accuracy of the solar sound speeds.

1) the value of the gravitational constant G is important for the standard solar models, 2) the value of G is not yet well determined by experiment, and 3) the value of this constant should be independently determined by helioseismological studies of the solar interior, especially in combination of the 8Be neutrino flux.

the uncertainties in G have important implications for the helioseismic determination of the sound speed and that the uncertainties in the sound speed can be reduced to the 1E-5 level in the near future.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implications for helioiseismology of the experimental uncertainties in Newton's constant.
the implications of the new value of Newton's constant G for solar models.
the determination of the solar neutrino fluxes and the implications for solar models, helioseismolgy and neutrino physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the helioseismic data are consistent with the standard solar model, and that the helioisemological results are consistent with the current values of G, but that a more precise determination of G is needed before a definitive conclusion can be made.

the solar neutrino flux measurements are not yet precise enough to distinguish among the various models of G, while helioseismological measurements of the square of sound speed are not yet precise to distinguish between the various models of the standard solar model.

the helioseismic data are consistent with a lower value of the gravitational constant, but that a more precise value of the gravitational coupling constant cannot be obtained with the present helioseismic measurements and solar model calculations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
helioseismological data is capable of providing a test of G to an accuracy of about 1 part in 10(6).
a 0.5% uncertainty in G leads to an uncertainty of the order of a few percent in the sound speed in a solar model.
the helioseismic constraints on the value of G are at least 10 times better than those from other astrophysical observations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncertainties in G are not a negligible source of uncertainty for the solar neutrino problem.
the uncertainties in G between experiments are important for helioseismic studies of the interior of the Sun.
helioseismological measurements can be used to independently test the value of Newton's constant.
